quote: Our analysis is based on the construction of an evaluation profile -a joint distribution of model behavior computed via evaluation/score functions on the distribution of model generations in response to (a set of) input prompts.
We study the prompt steerability of models, i.e., the extent to which a model can be steered via prompting alone.
outputs: Model responses (yes/no or free-form text) to profiling prompts under steering conditions.
The model generates yes/no responses to polar questions and free-form text in response to profiling and steering prompts.

quote: The score functions S, along with a set of prompts X ⊆ X , termed profiling prompts, yield a measure of a given language model's outputs, termed an evaluation profile. Formally, an evaluation profile is a joint distribution p X ∈ P = P (E), where p(s(x, y)) is the joint distribution of scores s(x, y) = (s 1 (x, y), . . . , s n (x, y)) for a given (x, y) pair.
The steerability indices are a proxy measure for how a model actually behaves under steering.
We define steerability indices that enable comparative measures of how much a model's profile changes on each dimension as a result of the number of steering statements (i.e., prompting effort).
